Contains 161 complete traditional poems and songs collecting the living oral memory of the Tangkhuls across agriculture, war, festivals, love, and mourning.

chapters.title: Creation, Origins & Ancestral Migration Songs
chapters.summary: The emergence from Wahukong (Hwang-Ho) and migration from Samsok to Hunphun.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Oh! hauri haura kachida haulu? Oh! hauri haura wahukongda haowa, Oh! wahukongda tunga. O Kachili Tunglo Awa Samshokli Tunga, O Makungana ili phunga, O Makunganao ili pangthan, Lungshang makang ana safasing sing, Mala mangli Hunphun Ava kharar. O Ram wungaphei, Shokvaoli wungho maya; Mei wungayar Hunphun wunga kharara.
chapters.english_translation: From what far valley did our ancestors emerge? From the river of Wahukong they journeyed. From Samsok in the east our lineage migrated, guided by the staves of Makungana. In Hunphun the ancestral fathers settled and lit the permanent council fires.
comprehension_questions: Where did Tangkhuls trace their ancient migration from?
What village was established as the mother-settlement?

chapters.title: Agricultural Cycles: Jhumming, Planting & Harvest
chapters.summary: Terrace work, transplantation songs (Luisom), and harvest celebration (Mahat).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kongrei mathei kongrei, kongrei shailo marei salo; Matei kachui manoye, Mala ifu heinao naoye. Ithanvara iram leisaye, Isu luisa khinasa, ima lera khinasa; Maleira souralo, isa luisa lung haorana. Zingkum leiyao leiyameirano, chungmeida kharshokrano, phungshon phungthaigei.
chapters.english_translation: The terrace waters ripple, transplant the green shoots with joyous songs! Sweet is the labor on our ancestral hills; who will share my buffalo meat and drink my rice beer? May our granaries be filled to the rafters and the year bring peace and plenty.
grammar_points: Imperative exhortation in communal work songs.
comprehension_questions: What food and drink are shared during terrace work?

chapters.title: Village Morung (Longra) & Dormitory Life Songs
chapters.summary: Longra drinking songs, companionship around the hearth, and youth solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Leader: I longnao (I Longra) ... ho...o...o! Members: Rapamlu ... ho...o...o! Machapralu ... ho...o...o! Sairam samjiya, sairam samjiya! Oh longra makazangwo, nawui shimli khisapamlo? Thakta razanglo, thakta razanglo!
chapters.english_translation: Leader: O comrades of the Longra! Members: Assemble, join the circle! Weep no more! The hunting grounds await our youth! Why linger solitary at home? Come swiftly into the warm circle of the dormitory hearth!
comprehension_questions: What social role did the Longra play in Tangkhul villages?
Describe the call-and-response structure of Song 38.

chapters.title: Historical Ballads: World War I & Regional Conflicts
chapters.summary: The 1917-18 France Labour Corps ballad and the 1919 Kuki War songs.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Rai ramli khava, rai ramli khava yaronpa, Yaronpa nakhi vasalo? Iya mavangai, sayisa sayi na tanti sahaowa. Franceshi ram khava, Franceli raikhavai; Makuiye makuiye, pham kata hiyo; Wungasam chap ngacha, rai ram khavayo. Ah khongjai rai khava yaronpa yaronva, Sangna ram penga yaronva; Kuiwung kuivaya suphung mei.
chapters.english_translation: Valiant young men journeying across distant seas to the battlefields of France in 1917; Putting on the soldier's uniform and marching into the unknown while elders lamented. In foreign lands they upheld the fearless reputation and honor of their ancestral hills.
grammar_points: Historical event dating embedded in oral songs.
comprehension_questions: What historical event is memorialized in Song 21?
How did Tangkhul communities respond to the 1917 call?

chapters.title: Romance, Courtship & Love Songs (Leishat Laa)
chapters.summary: Courtship dialogues, fishing expeditions, and declarations of enduring fidelity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Nana Kanta singloo, Ina Khailan singda, Kongli alei shonsa yahoo! Oh iwui sakhangai aluinao, kathuili oja saleiya aluinao; Mayo kachang tarn rahaira aluinao. Oh ini lungchang malai haosa, phaningda makhui aluinao leishiya; Kazingli samphangluinaosa aluinao.
chapters.english_translation: Take up your net and I will carry the line; together we shall cross the mountain stream! Beloved maiden, your smile brightens the terrace fields like springtime blossoms. Though our hands are parted here on earth, our souls are entwined forever in the sky.
grammar_points: First-person dual association in courtship songs.
comprehension_questions: What stream-fishing metaphor is used in courting?
How is fidelity expressed beyond mortality?

chapters.title: Festival Dances & Virgin Songs (Laa Khanganui)
chapters.summary: The sacred Luira dance performed by young maidens and festival elegance.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira sangai uwa, hoksa sangai uwa; Awungo Awunga shangrei rukchang ura, Yarui rukthang Kazing mathang ngaiyijile. Zingkam won wonluiya, ngalanao mawonluipaiya; Ngalanaowa mawon luipaiya, nathanram khavasangmeiya. Phaoli chan ma-ungkhararyo, haoriva haorava leiretnasaya.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira festival arrives, the feast of pork is spread! The Awunga and elders assemble in regal attire. Wildflowers bloom upon the slopes every spring, but human youth blossoms only once; Dance with joy in the courtyard while youth shines bright and the festival drums resound.
grammar_points: Metaphor of fleeting youth compared with floral seasons.
comprehension_questions: When is the Laa Khanganui performed?
What philosophical truth is contained in the floral metaphor?

chapters.title: Laments, Funerary Memorials & Philosophy
chapters.summary: Mourning over departed family and classical philosophical aphorisms.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Ili vaiphumlakha, Oh Ava khi mang shimanlo? Avayo khi mang shimanlo? Lengshongthei shimanna, Mayarnao mangna. Khamathan longli yurkathan masaralu, Ngaleizingli kapam sangmeiya (kazeiram); Khamna longli khangkaser masaralu, Ngaleizingli khyip sangmeiya.
chapters.english_translation: When grief engulfed me, what bright dream was lost? The pride of the lineage was cut down in youth. Boast not of wealth and pedigree on this mortal earth; beneath the ground in Kazeiram all sleep equally. Live in humility and kindness, for mortal life vanishes like morning mist on the ridges.
grammar_points: Prohibitive negative imperative -ralu in philosophical wisdom.
comprehension_questions: What moral counsel is given regarding wealth in Chapter 7?

chapters.title: Patriotic Anthems & Tribal Identity
chapters.summary: Celebration of the Tangkhul homeland, Longpi pottery, and the Shirui Lily.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Ngashan yanglo hey, Tangkhul ngalei hi! Kaphung kapha kongrei kongra hey, Khipana phashok Tangkhul ram? Varewui sokkhami ramna. Oh Tangkhul avaram, Tangkhul sinaram! Khangayam machining Irong sampunram, Ham kasa ram chiya Longpi ram na saya; Khamakang shim savai Hungpungram cement, Shirui ram lily mavatma nanaobing! Ringpha meiranu, mahomeiranu!
chapters.english_translation: Behold our glorious homeland! Mountains and crystal rivers bestowed by God. Beloved Tangkhul motherland! Longpi crafting timeless black stone-pottery, Hungpung building solid foundations, and Shirui Kashung blooming with the rare Shirui Lily! May prosperity and honor abide in our land forever!
comprehension_questions: Which village is celebrated for its pottery tradition?
What famous flower is native to Shirui Kashung?

colophon.title: The Tangkhul Folk Poetry in Song (HAOLA)

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Creation, Origins & Ancestral Migration Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Oh! hauri haura kachida haulu? Oh! hauri haura wahukongda haowa, Oh! wahukongda tunga. O Kachili Tunglo Awa Samshokli Tunga, O Makungana ili phunga, O Makunganao ili pangthan, Lungshang makang ana safasing sing, Mala mangli Hunphun Ava kharar. O Ram wungaphei, Shokvaoli wungho maya; Mei wungayar Hunphun wunga kharara.
excerpts.translation_en: From what far valley did our ancestors emerge? From the river of Wahukong they journeyed. From Samsok in the east our lineage migrated, guided by the staves of Makungana. In Hunphun the ancestral fathers settled and lit the permanent council fires.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Agricultural Cycles: Jhumming, Planting & Harvest
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kongrei mathei kongrei, kongrei shailo marei salo; Matei kachui manoye, Mala ifu heinao naoye. Ithanvara iram leisaye, Isu luisa khinasa, ima lera khinasa; Maleira souralo, isa luisa lung haorana. Zingkum leiyao leiyameirano, chungmeida kharshokrano, phungshon phungthaigei.
excerpts.translation_en: The terrace waters ripple, transplant the green shoots with joyous songs! Sweet is the labor on our ancestral hills; who will share my buffalo meat and drink my rice beer? May our granaries be filled to the rafters and the year bring peace and plenty.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Village Morung (Longra) & Dormitory Life Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Leader: I longnao (I Longra) ... ho...o...o! Members: Rapamlu ... ho...o...o! Machapralu ... ho...o...o! Sairam samjiya, sairam samjiya! Oh longra makazangwo, nawui shimli khisapamlo? Thakta razanglo, thakta razanglo!
excerpts.translation_en: Leader: O comrades of the Longra! Members: Assemble, join the circle! Weep no more! The hunting grounds await our youth! Why linger solitary at home? Come swiftly into the warm circle of the dormitory hearth!

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Historical Ballads: World War I & Regional Conflicts
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Rai ramli khava, rai ramli khava yaronpa, Yaronpa nakhi vasalo? Iya mavangai, sayisa sayi na tanti sahaowa. Franceshi ram khava, Franceli raikhavai; Makuiye makuiye, pham kata hiyo; Wungasam chap ngacha, rai ram khavayo. Ah khongjai rai khava yaronpa yaronva, Sangna ram penga yaronva; Kuiwung kuivaya suphung mei.
excerpts.translation_en: Valiant young men journeying across distant seas to the battlefields of France in 1917; Putting on the soldier's uniform and marching into the unknown while elders lamented. In foreign lands they upheld the fearless reputation and honor of their ancestral hills.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Romance, Courtship & Love Songs (Leishat Laa)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Nana Kanta singloo, Ina Khailan singda, Kongli alei shonsa yahoo! Oh iwui sakhangai aluinao, kathuili oja saleiya aluinao; Mayo kachang tarn rahaira aluinao. Oh ini lungchang malai haosa, phaningda makhui aluinao leishiya; Kazingli samphangluinaosa aluinao.
excerpts.translation_en: Take up your net and I will carry the line; together we shall cross the mountain stream! Beloved maiden, your smile brightens the terrace fields like springtime blossoms. Though our hands are parted here on earth, our souls are entwined forever in the sky.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Festival Dances & Virgin Songs (Laa Khanganui)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira sangai uwa, hoksa sangai uwa; Awungo Awunga shangrei rukchang ura, Yarui rukthang Kazing mathang ngaiyijile. Zingkam won wonluiya, ngalanao mawonluipaiya; Ngalanaowa mawon luipaiya, nathanram khavasangmeiya. Phaoli chan ma-ungkhararyo, haoriva haorava leiretnasaya.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira festival arrives, the feast of pork is spread! The Awunga and elders assemble in regal attire. Wildflowers bloom upon the slopes every spring, but human youth blossoms only once; Dance with joy in the courtyard while youth shines bright and the festival drums resound.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Ili vaiphumlakha, Oh Ava khi mang shimanlo? Avayo khi mang shimanlo? Lengshongthei shimanna, Mayarnao mangna. Khamathan longli yurkathan masaralu, Ngaleizingli kapam sangmeiya (kazeiram); Khamna longli khangkaser masaralu, Ngaleizingli khyip sangmeiya.
excerpts.translation_en: When grief engulfed me, what bright dream was lost? The pride of the lineage was cut down in youth. Boast not of wealth and pedigree on this mortal earth; beneath the ground in Kazeiram all sleep equally. Live in humility and kindness, for mortal life vanishes like morning mist on the ridges.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Ngashan yanglo hey, Tangkhul ngalei hi! Kaphung kapha kongrei kongra hey, Khipana phashok Tangkhul ram? Varewui sokkhami ramna. Oh Tangkhul avaram, Tangkhul sinaram! Khangayam machining Irong sampunram, Ham kasa ram chiya Longpi ram na saya; Khamakang shim savai Hungpungram cement, Shirui ram lily mavatma nanaobing! Ringpha meiranu, mahomeiranu!
excerpts.translation_en: Behold our glorious homeland! Mountains and crystal rivers bestowed by God. Beloved Tangkhul motherland! Longpi crafting timeless black stone-pottery, Hungpung building solid foundations, and Shirui Kashung blooming with the rare Shirui Lily! May prosperity and honor abide in our land forever!
